nodes.label: Working-Status API (planning-app feed)
nodes.rationale: Real-time feed of who is working right now with each employee's session start/end times for today plus the last 3 working days, designed for server-to-server consumption by the planning app.

nodes.label: WORKFORCE_API_KEY Shared-Secret Auth
nodes.rationale: The query-param form exists because the browser EventSource API cannot set custom headers. An unset key returns 503 - it fails closed because the feed contains staff PII.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events Snapshot Stream
nodes.rationale: SSE needs a long-running Node host; on short-lived serverless invocations the connection is capped, so callers poll the JSON endpoint instead. The JSON snapshot and the SSE snapshot frame share the exact same shape so a caller can switch freely.

nodes.label: Working-Status Snapshot Schema
nodes.rationale: Times are ISO-8601 UTC while calendar dates are Asia/Colombo days; current_session is a convenience mirror of the open session already present in days.

nodes.label: is_working Semantics (open session, overnight aware)
nodes.rationale: A session today with a check_in and no check_out counts; for is_shift_worker employees an open session that started yesterday also counts, because overnight shifts span midnight.

nodes.label: "Working Days" = Days With an Attendance Record
nodes.rationale: Weekends, holidays and leave days have no attendance record and are therefore skipped, so the 3 prior days returned are the 3 most recent days the person actually worked, looking back up to about three weeks.

nodes.label: Working-Status Operational Notes (PII, no-store, polling budget)
nodes.rationale: The feed contains personal data (email, phone) so responses are never cached and the key must stay secret. One snapshot is built from a single range query so polling is cheap, but callers should not poll faster than ~once every 10s - use SSE for sub-second freshness. EPF numbers can contain '/' and should be URL-encoded in the epf filter.
